turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about Owen's zero. Who decided it, and when?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
Eleven thirty-one, eleven fifty-two, eleven fifty-eight; I'm writing those down. Kids draft in one place and paste into another. And you still haven't told me who decided on the zero.
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine, Hale. Whatever happens next, this stays off Owen's record and it stays out of his classroom. Is anything on file right now?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Students misremember lines all the time. Turn it here; I'll search it myself. And you skipped my question: is anything on his file right now?
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
Okay. Nothing goes on his file, and nothing happens in front of his class. What exactly are you proposing?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't the same as having the book open at home. You've shown me three things, and I still don't have your proposal. Put it on the table, Hale.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

Then Owen does the rewrite, to put this behind him, privately and with nothing on his file. I want the date of the rewrite in tonight's email, and the new mark entered before December 1. His scholarship deadline doesn't move for anyone.
Will he do it?
He'll do it. Send me the date tonight, and make it after school.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed in our meeting to a private supervised rewrite of Owen's essay, not in front of his class, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require the date of the rewrite, after school, and the new mark entered before December 1. I expect your confirmation in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, and she still wants the date of the rewrite in tonight's email and the new mark entered before December 1; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and told her to read it herself, because it was specific, dated, tied to Owen's work and checkable.
What cost ground: You let her question about whether anything was already on his file go unanswered for several turns, which kept her pressing on procedure instead of on the evidence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, which is very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: The first time she asked whether anything was on his file, tell her plainly that nothing was and nothing would be, then go to your evidence.
